correctness.rationale: The open neighborhood splits into the row and column with the center removed. In a proper coloring each half uses any color at most once, and the center color is absent from both halves. Thus the colors of multiplicity one are precisely the symmetric difference of the two full palettes. The sizes are m and n, so for m<n every proper coloring works; row cliques force n colors and addition modulo n gives a proper n-coloring. For a square, an n-color palette must be exhausted in every row and column. In an (n+1)-color palette, a color used f times occupies exactly f rows and f columns, hence is omitted in the same number of rows and columns. Choose a color that some row omits: that row and an omitting column then have identical palettes. For the (n+2)-construction in the frozen proof, the two omitted-color pairs have cyclic differences ±2 and ±1, which are disjoint for n+2≥4. The construction works at n=2 as well, and an isolated singleton takes one color. These deductions establish the full range without using the optional finite coloring tests as proof.
residual_risks: The equivalence tested is for proper open-neighborhood colorings; it is not a statement about nonproper, closed-neighborhood or list variants.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In a proper rook coloring the possible multiplicities of a color in an open neighborhood are 0, 1 and 2, so there is an odd multiplicity exactly when there is a unique color. Under the line-graph correspondence the same condition is that the two endpoints of each edge have different incident-color sets in a proper edge coloring of K_m,n. These are equivalent tests, not different invariants here.

originality.rationale: Resultary fb9f4a963e44 states the same nontrivial rook formula and the same row/column palette criterion. Resultary 4827bdd1e654 additionally gives the identical result under odd coloring, which is equivalent on every proper rook coloring because every neighborhood color occurs at most twice. The excluded one-row case is a complete graph and the singleton is automatic, so neither supplies new mathematical content. This finding is materially covered regardless of priority between the same-day records or of the unresolved product-paper access.
residual_risks: Earliest priority not determined. Liu–Dou–Yang full text remained unavailable by the tried OA routes; no claim of noncoverage is made. Other primary literature on edge-coloring formulations may contain additional coverage, which is not needed for the decision.
